newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK parties as dignitaries dine at handover site.
newsitem.headline: HK parties as dignitaries dine at handover site.

text.p: As dignitaries dined and prepared to witness Hong Kong's historic transition to China, ordinary people packed the territory's streets and bars on Monday night for a final farewell to British colonial rule.
Despite on-and-off showers, a dazzling blast of fireworks lit up Victoria Harbour, drawing thousands of people to vantage points along the harbour front and across overpasses.

Crowds milling in the streets and spilling out of bars and restaurants lent Hong Kong the heady atmosphere of New Year's Eve or Chinese New Year. Hong Kong has been enjoying a five-day holiday declared to mark the handover.
In the Lan Kwai Fong entertainment area, hordes of people heading off to clubs mingled with couples in tuxedos and sequined gowns.
"We're just going to have a drink, hit the fireworks and head up to Club 64," said one British man who returned for a second tour of Hong Kong for the handover festivities.
"Where are the raves going on tonight?" asked a woman decked out in an elegant black dress for a company party.
Police kept an eye on the revellers crowding Lan Kwai Fong's narrow lanes -- the site of a crush on New Year's Eve 1992-93 that left 21 people dead -- but seemed to be keeping a low profile.
"It's chaos," said one man visiting from Sydney. "There are zillions of people down here."

Finding a taxi was nearly as tough as getting an invitation to the gala dinner and official ceremony at the Convention Centre where 4,000 VIPs were on hand to watch Britain's Prince Charles hand back Hong Kong to Chinese President Jiang Zemin at midnight, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.
